what: Martin Marietta supplies construction aggregates: crushed stone, sand and gravel from around 400 quarries, plus cement, ready-mixed concrete and asphalt. Aggregates produce the large majority of its profit.
customers: State transport departments building roads, infrastructure contractors, commercial developers and housebuilders.
money: crushed stone, sand and gravel across 28 states
moat: Quarries near the places that need the rock. Aggregates are too heavy to haul far economically, so each quarry has a local advantage that new permits rarely challenge.
risks: Debt of about $13 billion against almost no cash after acquisitions
Residential construction is weak while mortgage rates are high
Infrastructure volumes depend on government budgets
Return on invested capital of about 7% reflects the price paid for recent deals
opportunities: Revenue grew about 9% last year with a 23% operating margin
Aggregate prices have risen faster than costs for several years running
US infrastructure funding supports multi-year road and bridge demand
